login_description: Enter your credentials to access the console.
settings_language_desc: Interface language for this browser. Changing it reloads the page.
settings_appearance_desc: Color theme for this browser. Applies only to you.
settings_datetime_desc: How timestamps render across charts and history. Applies to everyone using this instance.
settings_admin_only: Only admins can change this setting.
auth_name_min: Name must be at least 2 characters
auth_password_min: Password must be at least 8 characters
auth_error_generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.
onboarding_admin_desc: This is the first account, so it becomes the administrator. Registration closes once it's created — add further users from Settings.
setup_subtitle: Choose a profile, test the connection, then activate it.
setup_activated_msg: {name} activated — restart the server to finish.
setup_activated_desc: The active profile shapes the API, manifest, and topics built once at boot, so it takes effect on the next restart.
setup_activate_desc: Activate {name} as this instance's inverter. This takes effect after the next server restart.
setup_no_profiles: No profiles available. Add an external source below to download one.
setup_download_more: Download more profiles from an external repository.
settings_subtitle: Manage how SunReye connects, records, and displays your system.
settings_sensors_desc: Hide sensors you don't use from this dashboard. Hidden sensors are still recorded and published to MQTT and the API — they only disappear from the web app.
settings_restart_failed: Server did not come back — restart the process manually, then reload.
access_public_desc: Let anyone view the live dashboard without signing in — for wall displays and kiosks. The dashboard is read-only: changing settings and controlling the inverter still require an admin login.
apikeys_toast_pick_user: Pick a user for the key
apikeys_revoke_confirm: Revoke key "{label}"? Applications using it will stop working.
apikeys_dialog_desc: This is the only time the full key is shown. Store it somewhere safe.
tariff_default_price_desc: Applied to any hour not covered by a time-of-use band below.
tariff_flat_rate_desc: Flat rate — every hour uses the default price. Add a band for time-of-use pricing.
inverter_simulate_pre: Running in simulation mode (set by the
inverter_simulate_post: environment variable). Connection settings below are saved but not used until simulation is turned off.
mqtt_enabled_desc: Bridge entities to an MQTT broker.
evcc_enabled_desc: Show your EVCC EV charger on the dashboard (uses the broker above).
evcc_topic_hint: Must match the "topic" setting in EVCC's mqtt configuration. EVCC must publish to the same broker.
evcc_subtract_hint: Split the EV out of the "Load" figure (shows Home = load − EV). Only enable if the charger is wired on the inverter's load output, so its draw is already inside the load reading.
weather_desc: Show current weather on the dashboard, from Open-Meteo (no account needed). Enter your location's coordinates — find them on any map service.
weather_toast_invalid_coords: Enter a valid latitude and longitude
weather_forecast_desc: Estimate your plant's output from the irradiance forecast for each panel orientation. Values come from the panel datasheet and your installation.
weather_forecast_arrays_empty: Add one entry per panel orientation (strings facing different directions get their own entry).
weather_forecast_azimuth_hint: Azimuth: 0 = south, -90 = east, 90 = west. Tilt: 0 = flat, 90 = vertical.
weather_forecast_clipping_desc: Once the battery is full, PV above your grid feed-in limit is curtailed. Set these so the forecast doesn't overstate output on bright days.
weather_forecast_toast_invalid: Enter valid numbers for every forecast field
weather_forecast_correction_desc: Learns your plant's systematic bias (shading, soiling, losses) from past production and nudges the forecast to match. It keeps learning in the background; enable to apply it.
weather_forecast_correction_empty: Still learning — correction factors appear here as production history builds up.
danger_restart_desc: Restart the server process to apply boot-time changes — chiefly a newly activated inverter profile, which reshapes the API, manifest, and topics built once at boot. Polling and live data pause briefly while it comes back.
danger_reset_desc: Permanently delete every recorded measurement — the raw history and all rollups behind the charts and cost pages — so the instance starts fresh. Accounts, settings, tariff, and profiles are kept. This cannot be undone.
danger_reset_confirm_pre: This permanently deletes all recorded measurements and cannot be undone. Type
danger_toast_reset_success: All measurement data cleared. Fresh data will appear as polling resumes.
profiles_restart_required: Restart required to apply profile changes.
profiles_restart_activate_pre: The server will restart to activate
profiles_restart_activate_post: . Polling and live data pause briefly while it comes back.
profiles_restart_generic: The server will restart to apply your profile changes. Polling and live data pause briefly while it comes back.
profiles_browse_hint: Browse your repositories to see profiles you can download.
profiles_none_found: No profiles found in the enabled repositories.
sources_url_invalid: URL must be an https git URL
snapshot_desc: {count} values read in {ms} ms. Check them for plausibility before saving.
statistics_subtitle: Costs, energy, prices and records for your system
statistics_tile_produced_explain: Total energy your panels generated over the period, and the daily average. The arrow compares it with the previous period of the same length.
statistics_tile_consumed_explain: Total energy your household used over the period, whether it came from solar, the battery or the grid.
statistics_tile_self_used_explain: Energy served on-site instead of imported: your consumption minus everything you had to buy from the grid.
statistics_tile_battery_charged_explain: Energy the battery took in over the period, from solar or the grid.
statistics_tile_battery_discharged_expla: Energy the battery gave back over the period. The gap to what it charged is round-trip loss.
statistics_heatmap_caption: Average per hour, folded onto one week
statistics_heatmap_summary: {metric} peaks on {weekday} around {hour}, averaging {amount} in that hour.
statistics_customize_hint: Pick what this page shows for everyone, then save.
statistics_records_vs_year: Compared with the same period a year ago
statistics_records_net_explain: What this period cost in total, against the reference period.
statistics_records_savings_explain: What solar saved and earned this period, against the reference period.
statistics_records_import_explain: Energy bought from the grid this period, against the reference period.
statistics_records_self_sufficiency_expl: Share of consumption covered on site, against the reference period.
statistics_records_max_production_explai: The single day your panels produced the most.
statistics_records_max_export_explain: The single day you sent the most energy to the grid.
statistics_records_max_load_explain: The single day the house used the most energy.
statistics_records_max_import_explain: The single day you bought the most energy from the grid.
statistics_records_best_self_sufficiency: The day the largest share of consumption came from your own system.
statistics_records_worst_self_sufficienc: The day the grid covered the largest share of consumption.
statistics_records_cheapest_day_explain: The day with the lowest all-in cost. Only covers the period prices are kept for.
statistics_records_priciest_day_explain: The day with the highest all-in cost. Only covers the period prices are kept for.
statistics_records_best_earnings_explain: The day exports earned the most. Only covers the period prices are kept for.
statistics_prices_history_truncated: Older windows fall outside the period prices are kept for.
statistics_prices_whatif: What a spot tariff would have cost
statistics_prices_whatif_note: Your imported energy repriced hour by hour and landed through your configured spot components. {coverage} of it had a market price.
statistics_prices_whatif_bare: Your tariff has no spot markup, grid fees, levies or VAT configured, so the spot figure is bare wholesale and understates a real bill.
statistics_prices_tile_avg_explain: Average wholesale price over this period, weighted by slot length. Not what you pay: a bill adds grid fees, levies and VAT on top.
statistics_prices_tile_min_explain: Lowest wholesale price of the period, and the day it happened.
statistics_prices_tile_max_explain: Highest wholesale price of the period, and the day it happened.
statistics_prices_tile_negative_hours_ex: Hours the market cleared below zero. Under §51 EEG a plant commissioned after 25 Feb 2025 earns nothing for energy exported then.
statistics_prices_tile_paid_explain: Wholesale price of the hours you actually imported in, weighted by how much you took. Below the market average means you bought at the cheaper times.
statistics_prices_tile_static_explain: What the energy you imported this period cost, priced with your tariff's time-of-use bands.
statistics_prices_tile_spot_explain: What the same energy would have cost priced hour by hour on the market. Hours with no stored price use your band price on both sides, so they cancel out.
statistics_prices_tile_delta_explain: Spot minus bands. A negative figure means a spot tariff would have been cheaper over this period.
toast_statistics_error: Failed to save the statistics layout
costs_tile_grid_cost_explain: What you actually pay the utility: imported energy priced at your tariff plus the standing charge. Export earnings are NOT subtracted here — this is the bill before feed-in income.
costs_tile_effective_cost_explain: Grid cost after subtracting export (feed-in) earnings — your net out-of-pocket for the period. Negative means feed-in outweighed your bill.
costs_tile_grid_import_explain: Energy drawn from the grid over the period, and what it cost to import.
costs_tile_grid_export_explain: Energy fed back to the grid over the period, and the feed-in earnings it produced.
costs_tile_solar_saving_explain: Value of solar/battery energy you used on-site instead of buying it: self-consumed kWh priced at the grid rate you would have paid. Excludes feed-in (that is Grid export).
costs_tile_total_savings_explain: How much better off you are than buying everything from the grid: solar saving plus export earnings. (Standing charge is excluded — you would pay it on all-grid too.)
costs_tile_self_sufficiency_explain: Share of your consumption covered by solar and battery over the period, instead of importing from the grid. 100% means you never touched the grid.
costs_tile_self_consumption_explain: Share of your solar production used on-site over the period, instead of exported to the grid. Higher means more of your solar went straight to your own load.
history_subtitle: Live and historical trends for every entity.
controls_subtitle: Writable settings for {name}. Changes are pushed to the inverter immediately.
controls_no_writable: This inverter exposes no writable settings.
controls_unlock_hint: Turn on to edit and push values to the inverter.
tou_schedule_desc_voltage: Six periods repeat every day; each runs until the next one starts. Each drives the battery toward a target voltage — with grid charge on it charges up to the target, otherwise it discharges down to it.
tou_schedule_desc_soc: Six periods repeat every day; each runs until the next one starts. Each drives the battery toward a target SOC — with grid charge on it charges up to the target, otherwise it discharges down to it.
tou_charges_hint: Charges from grid up to the target below
tou_discharges_hint: Discharges to load down to the target below
chart_no_data: No data for this range yet
chart_none_available: None of this chart's metrics are available in the active profile.
chart_metrics_unavailable_one: {count} metric unavailable in the active profile.
chart_metrics_unavailable_other: {count} metrics unavailable in the active profile.
chart_editor_desc: Overlay up to {count} metrics on a single chart.
logs_desc: Live server log stream. Pause to inspect the current output, or export it as a text file.
logs_no_match: No lines match the current filters.
automations_subtitle: Light control loops driven by live data and the solar forecast
automations_master_desc: Automations let SunReye write inverter settings on its own — today: peak shaving via the battery charge current. The master switch arms them; each automation is configured on the Automations page.
automations_disclaimer_body: Automations write inverter settings (battery max charge current) automatically. Make sure the configured limits match your hardware and grid contract — you remain responsible for your plant. SunReye restores your previous value whenever an automation lets go.
automations_toast_invalid: Enter valid numbers for all fields
automations_master_off_desc: Enable the master switch in Settings first.
automations_blockers_title: Cannot run with the current setup
automations_blocker_role_charge: The active profile maps no battery max charge current setting
automations_blocker_role_pv: The active profile maps no total PV power metric
automations_blocker_role_soc: The active profile maps no battery SOC metric
automations_blocker_export_limit: No export limit configured in the forecast settings.
automations_blocker_battery: No battery configured in the forecast settings.
peak_shaving_simulating_hint: Live simulation: peak shaving is off, but every tick still computes the decision it would make. Nothing is written to the inverter.
peak_shaving_shadow_desc: Decide and chart every tick without writing the inverter. Any register already held is handed back. Use it to check what peak shaving would do before letting it steer.
automations_charts_empty: Nothing recorded yet — one point is logged per tick while the automation runs.
automations_charts_retention: Kept in memory only: the last 24 hours, cleared when the server restarts.
automations_charts_live_hint: What the automation decided and wrote, next to what the plant did with it.
automations_charts_shadow_hint: Shadow run: these are the decisions peak shaving would have made. Nothing was written — compare the modelled export with the measured one in the tooltip.
automations_plan_today_hint: The day so far as measured — where the PV actually went — joined with the projection for what's left of it.
automations_plan_tomorrow_hint: Tomorrow replayed over its forecast. Tonight's drain into the house load is modelled down to the reserve floor; the load stays at its baseline and no car charges.
automations_plan_hint: The same rules replayed over the remaining forecast, carrying state of charge forward. It assumes the forecast holds and the house load stays at its baseline; it does not guess when a car will charge.
automations_plan_empty: No projection available — it needs a runnable setup, a solar forecast and fresh readings. Nothing left of today also shows up empty.
peak_shaving_desc: Steers the battery's max charge current from live PV, state of charge and the 15-minute forecast: surplus above the export limit charges the battery, and headroom is reserved for the midday peak.
peak_shaving_mode_exports_desc: The battery only absorbs power above the export limit; everything below it is sold. Charging falls back to the configured rate when the forecast peak can't fill the battery alone.
peak_shaving_mode_grid_desc: Lowers midday feed-in: the inverter is held at a dynamic export level and the battery is charged with the difference, so the export curve sits below the limit instead of pinned at it. PV above the export budget is given up — that is the price of the flatter curve. Needs the solar-sell max-power register.
peak_shaving_buffer_desc: Margin below the export limit at which shaving starts.
peak_shaving_max_charge_desc: Hard ceiling ever written to the inverter.
peak_shaving_fallback_desc: Rate used when no headroom must be reserved.
peak_shaving_floor_desc: Kept near full so the BMS can finish balancing; 0 disables.
peak_shaving_voltage_desc: Used for W→A when the profile maps no battery voltage.
peak_shaving_interval_desc: Seconds between control decisions — a register write happens at most this often.
peak_shaving_gf_min_threshold_desc: The plateau never drops below this, so some export keeps flowing. 0 lets the battery absorb everything.
peak_shaving_gf_trust_desc: How much of the forecast surplus is believed. Below 100 charges earlier, above 100 waits longer.
peak_shaving_gf_slew_desc: Caps how fast the threshold may move, damping a jumpy forecast. 0 disables.
peak_shaving_gf_charge_slew_desc: How fast the charge-current ceiling may move. Stepping from idle to the full ceiling swings kilowatts at the connection point, which is what this mode is meant to avoid. 0 is undamped.
peak_shaving_gf_ev_reserve_desc: Assume connected cars will eat today's surplus and charge the battery earlier. Off leaves that surplus to the car.
peak_shaving_ineffective_warning: The charge ceiling is being raised but the battery isn't absorbing — check the inverter's work mode (a sell-first mode overrides peak shaving).
peak_shaving_override_warning: The charge current was changed outside the automation — it will be overwritten on the next tick.
peak_shaving_no_forecast: Forecast unavailable — only live peak shaving is running.
peak_shaving_status_restore: Your previous charge current will be restored when the automation releases.
prices_tooltip_no_payment: No feed-in payment for this slot (§51 EEG)
prices_negative_summary_one: {hours} h of negative prices in one window — energy exported then earns nothing.
prices_negative_summary_other: {hours} h of negative prices across {windows} windows — energy exported then earns nothing.
prices_no_negative: No negative prices in this period.
prices_tomorrow_pending: Tomorrow's prices are not published yet — they clear around 13:00. Until then, nothing can be said about tomorrow's negative slots.
prices_hourly_source: This source only publishes hourly prices, so a negative quarter-hour inside a positive hour cannot be resolved.
prices_settings_intro: Fetch wholesale day-ahead prices for your market. Useful even on a fixed bill: under §51 EEG a plant commissioned after 25 Feb 2025 receives no feed-in payment for any quarter-hour whose price was negative.
prices_settings_publication: Tomorrow's prices clear around 13:00 market time and are fetched in the background; there is nothing to schedule.
prices_settings_error: Could not save the price source
tariff_marketing_eeg: Feed-in tariff, §51 (no payment when the price is negative)
tariff_marketing_desc: How exported energy is paid for. Needs a day-ahead price source to have any effect.
tariff_marketing_hint: Under §51 EEG a plant commissioned after 25 Feb 2025 is paid nothing for a quarter-hour whose day-ahead price was negative. Exporting then is worthless, not costly — so there is nothing to gain from curtailing, only from storing or consuming the energy instead. Under direct marketing a negative slot costs you money, and curtailing does pay.
tariff_management_fee_desc: Subtracted from the market price by your direct marketer.
tariff_import_follows_market_desc: Only for a spot-linked contract (Tibber, aWATTar, Ostrom …). Leave off for a fixed or time-of-use price.
automations_blocker_smart_meter: No smart meter gateway install date is set — price-aware charging is only meaningful once the 60 % cap has been lifted.
weather_smart_meter_since_desc: Date the iMSys was installed. Leave empty if you don't have one. Installing it is what lifts the 60 % feed-in cap, and it marks the plant as one §51 EEG applies to.
weather_export_cap_lifted: With a smart meter gateway the 60 % cap no longer applies — set the feed-in limit to 100 % of installed kWp (or your inverter's rating). Note that raising it leaves ordinary peak shaving with much less to do, which is what price-aware charging is for.
peak_shaving_pa_desc: Make room in the battery before a negative-price window and soak the surplus during it. Under §51 EEG energy exported then earns nothing, so storing it is the only way to keep its value. Needs a day-ahead price source.
peak_shaving_pa_needs_smart_meter: Set a smart meter gateway install date under Weather & Forecast first — §51 only applies to plants that have one.
peak_shaving_pa_enable_desc: Off leaves peak shaving exactly as it was; windows are still shown on the Statistics screen.
peak_shaving_pa_shape: Hold the battery low before a window
peak_shaving_pa_shape_desc: Charge as much as possible, as late as possible, so the pack arrives with room. Off still soaks during the window itself.
peak_shaving_pa_threshold_desc: A slot at or below this counts as negative. 0 is the §51 rule exactly.
peak_shaving_pa_min_window_desc: Ignore windows shorter than this — a single stray slot isn't worth steering for.
peak_shaving_pa_lookahead_desc: How far in advance the battery starts making room.
peak_shaving_pa_soak_floor_desc: 0 absorbs everything the pack can take; higher keeps some export flowing.
peak_shaving_pa_margin_desc: Aim this much below the SOC the window needs. Arriving slightly too empty costs little; arriving too full wastes the window.
peak_shaving_spend_down_hint: The battery is already fuller than the coming window needs. Withholding charge alone can't empty it in time — shifting flexible load (EV, hot water) into the window is what closes the gap.
peak_shaving_pa_pull_in_ev: Use the car as a sink
peak_shaving_pa_pull_in_ev_desc: Borrow connected chargers as a sink during a negative-price window: wake an idle charger onto surplus charging, and — while the battery is too full to make room on its own — switch on EVCC's battery boost so the car empties it. Everything is handed back afterwards. A charger you left on immediate charging is never touched.
peak_shaving_pa_ev_boost_limit_desc: How far the car may empty the house battery while boosting. EVCC holds the battery here rather than letting it oscillate; the plant's own reserve floor still applies on top.
costs_tile_zero_value_explain: Energy exported during quarter-hours whose day-ahead price was negative. Under §51 EEG a plant commissioned after 25 Feb 2025 receives no feed-in payment for it. Storing or consuming that energy instead is the only way to keep its value.
peak_shaving_pa_grid_charge: Charge the battery from the grid
peak_shaving_pa_grid_charge_desc: Buy from the grid during a window. Only has any effect when your import price follows the market (Settings → Tariff) — a negative wholesale price does not lower a fixed bill. Even then you still pay grid fees, levies and VAT, so this is about buying at the cheapest hour, not about being paid to consume.
peak_shaving_pa_grid_charge_a_desc: Current drawn from the grid while charging in a window.
